title: Roadmap
summary: The state of the art year by year to the 2040s, tagged by how certain it is.

ideas.how: CFET and 2D materials are the next answers

measures.how: the roadmap names nodes year by year

then: Everything after 2026 on the roadmap is a plan or a projection.

challenges.title: Travel to 1985
challenges.task: Set the time machine to 1985 and find which of today's topics and companies did not exist yet.

learn.plain: Chips used to get better mainly by shrinking. Now they improve by stacking, smarter packaging, faster memory and new materials. The roadmap is a best guess that gets revised every year.
learn.engineer: Through 2030 most density gains come from shorter standard cells, backside power and CFET rather than gate-pitch scaling, which imec expects to stay near 42 nm from A10 to A5. Beyond that, 2D channels, Hyper-NA EUV and 3D integration are the main levers, while system-level gains come from co-designing packaging, memory and interconnect.

quiz.q: Around when does imec expect CFET transistors to arrive?
quiz.why: It is a research projection, so it may move.

quiz.q: What did Intel ship first using High-NA EUV in 2026?
options: Select layers of Panther Lake processors on Intel 18A
quiz.why: ASML announced the milestone in July 2026.

quiz.q: On the roadmap, what does "Projection" mean?
options: A research forecast that may change
quiz.why: Shipping, announced, projection and outlook tell you how much to trust each item.
